title: The Giant Squids of the Jurassic Period - Nautilus
gist: A Papers in Palaeontology study by US, UK and New Zealand researchers describes Wyoteuthis linsterorum, a new belemnite species from the Jurassic "Sundance Sea" that once flooded Wyoming, named for the late amateur collector Cliff Linster.

themes.theme: A sea where Wyoming is now

insights.claim: Around 160 million years ago, rising global sea levels sent the Pacific Ocean flooding into what is now Wyoming, creating the "Sundance Sea" whose sediments have yielded countless fossils of extinct ammonites and belemnites.
insights.so_what: A concrete deep-time datum on how far continental interiors flood under sustained sea-level rise.
insights.locator: It’s hard to picture a squid in Wyoming
insights.speaker: Devin Reese

insights.claim: A new study in Papers in Palaeontology by researchers from the U.S., U.K. and New Zealand reports two fossils of a belemnite with particularly unusual characteristics, describing the new species Wyoteuthis linsterorum.
insights.so_what: Establishes provenance for the claim and shows how thin the specimen base can be for a formal new species description — two fossils.
insights.locator: Now, a new study published in Papers in Palaeontology
insights.speaker: Devin Reese

insights.claim: The species name honors the late fossil collector Cliff Linster, who personally found the second specimen, showing that amateur collectors still supply material for formal paleontological description.
insights.so_what: Private and amateur collection remains a real input to the scientific record, which cuts both ways for fossil-market regulation debates.
insights.quote: honors late fossil collector Cliff Linster who found the second specimen
insights.locator: The name of the new species
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
